conviction_note: Median reaction 15.97% with only two of seven up and the last two prints at -28.64% and -22.13%, into a stock 92.66% below its 52-week high that jumped 11% pre-market the day before the print on an automated Wall Street Zen rating change while the corpus's retail base was explicitly positioning for an earnings run-up; about a fifth of the median, negative.

findings.finding: The immediate pre-print gain in this name had a named and low-quality cause: the stock was 'up 11% pre-market on Wall Street Zen upgrade' on 2026-09-01, an algorithmic rating service rather than an information event, arriving on top of a retail base that had spent the prior fortnight explicitly buying for the print ('we should see a good run up next week following into the ER', 'a good earnings and we are back at $8-9') at a company whose last two prints produced -28.64% and -22.13% and which has disappointed on five of its last seven.
findings.corpus_ref: docs/cc13cba0f406c306d3e28b6d98b95c2f8eb70731.txt (sweep 20260901T150611Z), message of 2026-09-01T12:49:56Z for the upgrade and the 11% pre-market move; docs/d0ef63de40a499161bef78aee98c50d1a8e51eb0.txt (sweep 20260830T083705Z) for the run-up positioning at 2026-08-21T14:44:11Z, 2026-08-26T19:53:20Z and 2026-08-27T09:26:56Z; the reaction record is baselines/ZEPP.json. The URL given is the only third-party link in the corpus that is not a retail post, since the upgrade itself has no captured source
findings.why_not_priced: An 11% pre-market move on a quant rating change at a stock with 41,540 shares of average daily volume is a liquidity artefact, not a re-rating, and nothing in the capture aggregates the fact that the froth going into this print is mechanical. The corpus's genuine positive datapoints - an Amazfit athlete winning UTMB, a half-marathon world record set on an unsponsored Cheetah 2 Pro, Balance 3 titanium sold out on the US site, an Amazon marketplace tie-up, roughly $4m a quarter of debt paydown toward the first debt-free year since leaving Xiaomi - are brand and balance-sheet items, not revenue in the reported quarter, and the corpus itself concedes 'might not yet be inflection point'. On a company doing about $300m of annual revenue, five disappointments in seven prints is the base rate, and it is being met with a book that has just been marked up by an algorithm. The band is wide and reaches +10 because two of the seven prints delivered +34.00% and +15.33% and because a 92.66% drawdown means the bar is genuinely low.
findings.independence: From a different source in the same corpus and pulling the other way, which is why the upside band is open: the product and athlete evidence at 2026-08-24T14:37:34Z and 2026-08-29T13:29:41Z, and the observation at 2026-08-19T14:41:40Z that 'expectations vs price isn't high'. Nothing in the filings index corroborates or contradicts the finding.

searched_and_found_nothing: the Wall Street Zen note itself or any recognised sell-side action: neither is in the capture, so the upgrade reaches me only as a retail report of its price effect
any company filing in the run-in that I could score: this is a foreign private issuer filing 6-Ks and I found nothing in the window that bears on the print
a consensus revenue or EPS estimate, or any preview from a recognised source

confirmation of the print date from a company source: the capture directory is dated 2026-09-01 while the baseline says 2026-09-02, and the corpus contains retail messages pointing at both ('Financial results 1st sept', 'tomorrow earnings call' posted 2026-08-31)
hard numbers behind the debt-paydown and cash claims, or any quantification of the US-market push
a shipment, sell-through or Amazon-ranking datapoint for the June quarter
baseline_tension: It sits with the five-day run-up of -11.59% only loosely, since that number predates the 11% bounce, and it agrees squarely with the reaction history: two up out of seven, the last two both worse than -22%. The 20-day run-up of -0.44% conceals both the fall and the bounce, which is part of why the pre-print positioning read matters here.
corpus_limits: The print date is ambiguous in this capture - the directory is named for 2026-09-01 and the baseline for 2026-09-02 - and no clean-view file exists for ZEPP. I treated the 2026-09-01T15:06:11Z sweep as admissible because its content contains no results whatsoever, only an upgrade-driven price move, which is the operative test; if the print was in fact 2026-09-01 bmo then that sweep should be excluded and this finding falls away. No option chain or skew. Average daily volume of 41,540 shares means the tape is close to uninformative. No news documents and no stored filing bodies; the baseline's reaction history rests on a 6-K text heuristic rather than item codes.
